(sec-item-markerbodyuser)=
# MarkerBodyUser

A marker on any number of bodies whose position, and with providedMarkerType Position | Orientation its rotation, are computed by Python user functions from the coordinates of the nodes of these bodies, e.g. a point between several bodies or nodes, or a point of a mesh. Loads, connectors, joints and sensors use it as a position or rigid marker; a connector or joint on it needs its Jacobian functions (#3107).

## Interface

- Provides: `Position`, `Orientation`
- Bodies it can be placed on: [](#sec-item-objectground), [](#sec-item-objectmass1d), [](#sec-item-objectrotationalmass1d), [](#sec-item-objectrigidbody), [](#sec-item-objectrigidbody2d), [](#sec-item-objectuserbody), [](#sec-item-objectffrf), [](#sec-item-objectffrfreducedorder), [](#sec-item-objectancfcable2d), [](#sec-item-objectaleancfcable2d), [](#sec-item-objectancfbeam), [](#sec-item-objectbeamgeometricallyexact2d), [](#sec-item-objectbeamgeometricallyexact), [](#sec-item-objectancfthinplate)
- Connectors, constraints and loads that can use it: [](#sec-item-objectconnectorspringdamper), [](#sec-item-objectconnectorcartesianspringdamper), [](#sec-item-objectconnectorrigidbodyspringdamper), [](#sec-item-objectconnectorlinearspringdamper), [](#sec-item-objectconnectortorsionalspringdamper), [](#sec-item-objectconnectorgravity), [](#sec-item-objectconnectorhydraulicactuatorsimple), [](#sec-item-objectjointuser), [](#sec-item-objectconnectordistance), [](#sec-item-objectconnectorrollingdiscpenalty), [](#sec-item-objectcontactconvexroll), [](#sec-item-objectcontactspheresphere), [](#sec-item-objectcontactspheretorus), [](#sec-item-objectcontactspheretriangle), [](#sec-item-objectcontactspherecylinder), [](#sec-item-objectcontactcylindercylinder), [](#sec-item-objectcontactconecone), [](#sec-item-objectcontactconetriangle), [](#sec-item-objectcontactconvexconvex), [](#sec-item-objectcontactprimitiveconvex), [](#sec-item-objectcontactcylindertriangle), [](#sec-item-objectjournalbearing), [](#sec-item-objectcontactcurvecircles), [](#sec-item-objectjointgeneric), [](#sec-item-objectjointrevolutez), [](#sec-item-objectjointprismaticx), [](#sec-item-objectjointspherical), [](#sec-item-objectjointrollingdisc), [](#sec-item-objectjointrevolute2d), [](#sec-item-objectjointprismatic2d), [](#sec-item-loadforcevector), [](#sec-item-loadtorquevector)

## Parameters

The parameters of the item; in a dictionary, its type is 'BodyUser':

| name | type | size | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **name** | String |  | '' | marker's unique name |
| **bodyNumbers** | ArrayObjectIndex |  | [] | (symbol: $[b_0,\,b_1,\,\ldots]\tp$) the bodies whose coordinates the user functions get, at least one |
| **providedMarkerType** | MarkerType |  | MarkerType.Position | what the marker provides besides Body and Object: exu.MarkerType.Position, or exu.MarkerType.Position \| exu.MarkerType.Orientation with the rotationMatrixUserFunction |
| **parameters** | NumpyVector |  | [] | (symbol: $\pv_{par} \in \Rcal^{n_p}$) the parameters of the marker, of any length, passed to the user functions; see exudyn.advancedUtilities.ParameterLayout |
| **positionUserFunction** | MarkerBodyUserPositionUserFunction |  | 0 | (symbol: $\LU{0}{\pv}(\qv)$) A Python user function which computes the global position of the marker; it must be given |
| **positionJacobianUserFunction** | MarkerBodyUserPositionJacobianUserFunction |  | 0 | (symbol: $\Jm_{pos}(\qv) \in \Rcal^{3\times n}$) A Python user function which computes the position Jacobian; required if a connector or joint is on the marker, else when it is needed |
| **rotationMatrixUserFunction** | MarkerBodyUserRotationMatrixUserFunction |  | 0 | (symbol: $\LU{0m}{\Rot}(\qv) \in \Rcal^{3\times 3}$) A Python user function which computes the rotation matrix of the marker; given exactly for providedMarkerType Position \| Orientation |
| **rotationJacobianUserFunction** | MarkerBodyUserRotationJacobianUserFunction |  | 0 | (symbol: $\Jm_{rot}(\qv) \in \Rcal^{3\times n}$) A Python user function which computes the rotation Jacobian (of the global angular velocity); required if a connector or joint on the marker requests the orientation, else when it is needed |
| **visualization** | VMarkerBodyUser |  |  | parameters for visualization of item |

## Visualization parameters

The parameters of `VMarkerBodyUser`, given as `visualization`:

| name | type | size | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **show** | Bool |  | True | set true, if item is shown in visualization and false if it is not shown |

## Drawing

Drawn as [all markers](#sec-drawing-markers).
(description-markerbodyuser)=
## Detailed description

### Coordinates and user functions

The marker acts on the coordinates of the nodes of its bodies, body by body in the order of `bodyNumbers`, and for
each body in the order of its nodes - $\qv \in \Rcal^n$, as a connector on the marker gets them (#3065). The user
functions get the reference coordinates `qRef`, the total coordinates `qTotal` (reference plus displacement), the
velocities `q_t` and the `parameters`, as those of NodeUser and ObjectUserBody do.

| user function | gives | needed for |
|---|---|---|
| `positionUserFunction` | $\LU{0}{\pv}(\qv)$ | always |
| `positionJacobianUserFunction` | $\Jm_{pos} = \partial \LU{0}{\pv} / \partial \qv \in \Rcal^{3 \times n}$ | the velocity, forces; required at Assemble if a connector or joint is on the marker (#3107) |
| `rotationMatrixUserFunction` | $\LU{0m}{\Rot}(\qv)$ | providedMarkerType Position \| Orientation: joints, torques |
| `rotationJacobianUserFunction` | $\Jm_{rot} = \partial \LU{0}{\tomega} / \partial \dot\qv \in \Rcal^{3 \times n}$ | the angular velocity, torques; required at Assemble if a connector or joint on the marker requests the orientation |

The velocity is $\Jm_{pos} \dot \qv$, the angular velocity $\Jm_{rot} \dot \qv$. A force $\fv$ on the marker gives
the generalized forces $\Jm_{pos}\tp \fv$, a torque $\Jm_{rot}\tp \mv$.

### Marker type

`providedMarkerType` says what the marker provides, besides Body and Object (#3103): `exu.MarkerType.Position`, the
default, or `exu.MarkerType.Position | exu.MarkerType.Orientation` for a rigid marker. Position | Orientation needs
the rotationMatrixUserFunction, and a rotation function given with Position alone is refused at Assemble; a joint
or a torque on a marker of type Position is refused as on any position marker. The user functions
are called serially, in the main thread; the marker and what depends on it are drawn in the main thread. What
needs a Jacobian function that is not given raises, the Jacobians are not approximated (#3107); the Jacobians of
connectors on the marker are computed numerically.

**Userfunction**: `positionUserFunction(mbs, t, itemNumber, qRef, qTotal, q_t, parameters)`
A user function, which computes the global position of the marker from the coordinates of its bodies.

| arguments / return | type or size | description |
|---|---|---|
| `mbs` | MainSystem | provides MainSystem mbs to which the marker belongs |
| `t` | Real | time of the configuration asked for |
| `itemNumber` | Index | integer number of the marker in mbs |
| `qRef` | Vector $\in \Rcal^n$ | the reference coordinates of the nodes of the bodies, body by body in the order of bodyNumbers and of the nodes of each body |
| `qTotal` | Vector $\in \Rcal^n$ | the total coordinates of these nodes - reference plus displacement coordinates - of the configuration asked for |
| `q_t` | Vector $\in \Rcal^n$ | the velocity coordinates of these nodes; zero in the reference configuration |
| `parameters` | Vector $\in \Rcal^{n_p}$ | the parameters of the marker, see parameters; empty if not given |
| **return value** | Vector3D $\in \Rcal^{3}$ | the global position of the marker |

A Python user function gets its vector and matrix arguments as read-only numpy arrays, valid during the call, see [](#sec-userfunctions).

**Userfunction**: `positionJacobianUserFunction(mbs, t, itemNumber, qRef, qTotal, q_t, parameters)`
A user function of the marker that returns a matrix: the position Jacobian $\Jm_{pos} = \partial \vv / \partial \dot\qv$ (3 x n), the rotation matrix (3 x 3) or the rotation Jacobian $\Jm_{rot} = \partial \LU{0}{\tomega} / \partial \dot\qv$ (3 x n, global angular velocity).

| arguments / return | type or size | description |
|---|---|---|
| `mbs` | MainSystem | provides MainSystem mbs to which the marker belongs |
| `t` | Real | time of the configuration asked for |
| `itemNumber` | Index | integer number of the marker in mbs |
| `qRef` | Vector $\in \Rcal^n$ | the reference coordinates of the nodes of the bodies, body by body in the order of bodyNumbers and of the nodes of each body |
| `qTotal` | Vector $\in \Rcal^n$ | the total coordinates of these nodes - reference plus displacement coordinates - of the configuration asked for |
| `q_t` | Vector $\in \Rcal^n$ | the velocity coordinates of these nodes; zero in the reference configuration |
| `parameters` | Vector $\in \Rcal^{n_p}$ | the parameters of the marker, see parameters; empty if not given |
| **return value** | MatrixContainer | the matrix, as numpy array or list of lists |

A Python user function gets its vector and matrix arguments as read-only numpy arrays, valid during the call, see [](#sec-userfunctions).

**Userfunction**: `rotationMatrixUserFunction(mbs, t, itemNumber, qRef, qTotal, q_t, parameters)`
A user function of the marker that returns a matrix: the position Jacobian $\Jm_{pos} = \partial \vv / \partial \dot\qv$ (3 x n), the rotation matrix (3 x 3) or the rotation Jacobian $\Jm_{rot} = \partial \LU{0}{\tomega} / \partial \dot\qv$ (3 x n, global angular velocity).

| arguments / return | type or size | description |

A Python user function gets its vector and matrix arguments as read-only numpy arrays, valid during the call, see [](#sec-userfunctions).

(miniexample-markerbodyuser)=
## Mini example


```python
#a marker at the midpoint of two mass points, held by a spring to the ground
nA = mbs.AddNode(NodePoint(referenceCoordinates=[-0.5,0,0], initialCoordinates=[0,0.1,0]))
nB = mbs.AddNode(NodePoint(referenceCoordinates=[0.5,0,0], initialCoordinates=[0,0.1,0]))
bA = mbs.AddObject(MassPoint(nodeNumber=nA, mass=1))
bB = mbs.AddObject(MassPoint(nodeNumber=nB, mass=1))
def UFposition(mbs, t, itemNumber, qRef, qTotal, q_t, parameters):
    return 0.5*(qTotal[0:3] + qTotal[3:6])
def UFpositionJacobian(mbs, t, itemNumber, qRef, qTotal, q_t, parameters):
    return 0.5*np.hstack((np.eye(3), np.eye(3)))
mMid = mbs.AddMarker(MarkerBodyUser(bodyNumbers=[bA, bB], positionUserFunction=UFposition,
                                    positionJacobianUserFunction=UFpositionJacobian))
mGround = mbs.AddMarker(MarkerBodyPosition(bodyNumber=oGround))
k = 100
mbs.AddObject(CartesianSpringDamper(markerNumbers=[mGround, mMid], stiffness=[k,k,k]))

mbs.Assemble()
mbs.SolveDynamic()

#the midpoint oscillates with omega = sqrt(k/(2 m)), from 0.1: 0.1*cos(omega) at t=1
exu.sys['testResult'] = mbs.GetMarkerOutput(mMid, exu.OutputVariableType.Position)[1]
```
